records.name: St. Paul's Episcopal Church
records.summary: An Episcopal parish in Chestnut Hill with three Sunday services and choirs of almost 80 singers across adults and children. It also runs a youth program and a monthly collection for local partner agencies.
records.what_you_do: Sit in on a Sunday service, ask about the choirs or the youth program (S.P.Y.), or bring an item to the monthly collection for a partner agency.

schedule.text: Sunday services at 8 am (quiet spoken Eucharist), 9 am (family service on the labyrinth) and 11 am (choral Eucharist), plus Sunday evening services at 5 or 7 pm as scheduled.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: the Chestnut Hill East or Chestnut Hill West Regional Rail station, each about one block away. The number 23 bus ends about a half block away.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday service and pick up a visitor card at the registration table in the narthex, or call 215-242-2055 to ask about the choirs or the youth program.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, encourages visitors to try more than one service, and has visitor cards at the narthex table. The choir page also lists steps for getting started. It has no formal newcomer class.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services are open to anyone of any age, and the site suggests trying a few to find the one that suits you. The 8 am service is quiet and spoken, with no hymns. The 9 am service is informal and aimed at families, and the 11 am service has hymns, choral anthems and a sermon. Coffee hour follows the 11 am service in Dixon House, and from September to May a Sunday breakfast runs from 8:30 to 9:30 am in the Parish Hall for a small donation.
first_visit_tips: Pick up a visitor card at the registration table in the narthex.
Parking is in the driveway lot, the stone lot behind Dixon House, or on the street along Bethlehem Pike and Chestnut Hill Avenue.
Stay for coffee hour in Dixon House after the 11 am service.
Call 215-242-2055 with questions about accessibility, since the site does not describe it.

records.notes: The site has no separate join, visit or new-here page. The choir page links to a Choral Auditions page that I did not open, so whether beginners can join the choirs is unknown. The 2025 Thanksgiving Turkey Drive is dated only by year, so no month is recorded and last_sign_of_life is not set. The Sunday evening schedule is on a separate weekly page I did not open. Accessibility is not described on the site.

records.name: St. Peter the Apostle Parish
records.summary: A Redemptorist Catholic parish at 5th Street and Girard Avenue, home to the National Shrine of St. John Neumann. It offers Mass most days, including a Spanish Mass on Sundays.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, the Wednesday novena to Our Lady of Perpetual Help at 7 pm, or a visit to the National Shrine of St. John Neumann.

schedule.text: Saturday Masses at 12:15 pm and 5:30 pm (vigil). Sunday Masses at 7:30 am, 9:30 am, 11 am (Spanish) and 12:30 pm. Weekday Masses at 7 am, 12:15 pm and 5:30 pm. Confession Monday to Saturday at 11:45 am and 5 pm, and Sunday at 10:30 am in Spanish. Wednesday novena to Our Lady of Perpetual Help at 7 pm.

locations.label: National Shrine of St. John Neumann (rectory address)

first_step.how: Come to any Mass on the schedule, or call the rectory at 215-627-2386 to arrange a visit with a priest.
first_step.basis: The March 2026 parish bulletin calls the parish welcoming and diverse and asks people to make an appointment by phone with a priest. The parish website could not be opened, and no newcomer program is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and the 11 am Sunday Mass is in Spanish, so choose the time that fits your language. If you want to talk with a priest, the bulletin asks you to make an appointment by phone first. Weekday Masses are at 7 am, 12:15 pm and 5:30 pm.
first_visit_tips: Call the rectory at 215-627-2386 before you come if you want to meet a priest.
Confession is offered Monday to Saturday at 11:45 am and 5 pm, and on Sunday at 10:30 am in Spanish.
The rectory office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm.
The parish listing does not describe parking or transit, so ask the rectory before you come.

records.notes: The parish website (spaphilly.org) returned HTTP 500 on three tries, so this record rests on the weekly bulletin dated March 22, 2026, which is hosted on the parish site, plus the archdiocese listing carried over from tier 1 (shrine visiting hours and the Wednesday novena day were not re-read). The bulletin's Saturday and Sunday times replace the tier 1 times. An older archdiocese listing and a 2014 article mention a 3:30 pm Sunday Mass with novena and a Tuesday 7 pm Spanish Mass; the March 2026 bulletin does not list these, so they are left out. A search result also mentioned a 7:30 am Sunday Mass that the bulletin confirms.

records.name: St. Philip Neri Parish
records.summary: The Catholic parish in Queen Village at 218 Queen Street, with a Saturday vigil at 4:30 pm, a 10 am Sunday Mass, and weekday Masses at 7:30 am. The parish office helps new parishioners register and start RCIA.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday Mass at 10 am or a weekday Mass, or call the parish office about registering, baptism classes, or RCIA (the program for adults who want to join the Catholic Church).

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Sunday Mass at 10 am. Weekday Mass at 7:30 am, Monday to Friday. Saturday confession 3:45 to 4:15 pm, and Sunday confession before the 10 am Mass. Holy day Mass at 7:30 am, with a holy day vigil at 7 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass, or call the parish office at 215-468-1922 to register or ask about RCIA, which starts each fall for people over 14.
first_step.basis: The contact page opens with a hello and welcome, lists what newcomers can start (registering, RCIA, baptism), and gives the office number. Mass itself needs no sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and the Sunday 10 am Mass is the one the site lists for visitors. For registration, RCIA or baptism, the office asks you to call first. Office hours are weekdays from 9 am to 4 pm.
first_visit_tips: Call the office on a weekday between 9 am and 4 pm if you want to register or ask about RCIA.
Sunday confession is offered before the 10 am Mass, and Saturday confession runs 3:45 to 4:15 pm.
The site does not describe parking or transit, so ask the office if you need those details.

records.notes: The site shows no dated news, so status stays probably_active. The site does not list holy day times, so the holy day line is carried over from tier 1 (archdiocese listing, not re-read). The site also names St. Stanislaus Church at 242 Fitzwater Street as part of the parish's history; it is a church site, not a separate group, and was not checked.

records.name: St. Raymond of Penafort Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Williams Avenue and Vernon Road with Sunday Masses at 8 and 10 am and weekday Masses at 8 am. Its ministries include altar servers, readers, a Bethany welcome team, and outreach to people who are hungry or are refugees.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, join the Bethany welcome team or a life group, or sign up for a ministry such as altar serving, reading, or music. Outreach includes Feed The Hungry and Refugee Support.

schedule.text: Saturday Masses at 5 pm and 8 am. Sunday Masses at 8 am and 10 am. Weekday Mass at 8 am on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday (the site lists no Wednesday Mass). Saturday confession 4 to 4:45 pm or by appointment, and Sunday confession 9:30 to 9:50 am.

first_step.how: Come to the 10 am Sunday Mass, then call the rectory at 215-549-3760 to ask about a life group or the Bethany team, or use the parish volunteer form.
first_step.basis: The site has an I'm New section, the Bethany team helps make weekend Mass welcoming, and the life groups page invites newcomers to join a group and says how to ask. The welcome and join pages did not open, so the rating rests on the pages that did.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, with Sunday Masses at 8 and 10 am and a Saturday Mass at 5 pm. Life groups are small groups of about 5 to 12 people who read the coming Sunday's Scriptures together and get to know one another; they form a few times a year. The site does not say whether groups take drop-ins, so ask first.
first_visit_tips: Call the rectory at 215-549-3760 to ask about life groups and the Bethany team, since the site does not say whether groups take drop-ins.
Saturday confession runs 4 to 4:45 pm, and you can also book a time by appointment.
The site does not describe parking or wheelchair access, so ask before you come if you need those details.

records.notes: The welcome, join and join-our-parish pages returned 404 at guessed addresses, so the newcomer path is built from the life groups and ministries pages and the home page menu. The Sunday 9:30 am confession time and the cost line are carried over from the tier 1 archdiocese listing (not re-read). The home page lists Saturday Mass at 8 am among the weekday Masses. The life group contact is a named staff member; I did not record a personal email.

records.name: St. Richard Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 18th and Pollock Streets in South Philadelphia, serving Catholics since 1924. It has a Saturday vigil, Sunday Masses at three times (one at the Holy Spirit worship site), and a faith formation program (PREP) for children.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, register as a new parishioner online or in person, or ask about faith formation (PREP) for children and teens.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm at St. Richard. Sunday Masses at 8 am and 11:30 am at St. Richard, and at 10 am at the Holy Spirit worship site. Weekday Masses at 8:30 am, Monday to Saturday. Holy days are announced ahead of time. Confession Saturdays 3:30 to 4:15 pm and before Sunday Masses.

first_step.how: Come to any Mass on the schedule, or register as a new parishioner through the online form on the parish site, or visit the rectory at 3010 S. 18th Street.
first_step.basis: The Register page walks new households through the form and closes with a welcome, and the home page invites visitors to come and see. The parish also accepts registration in person at the rectory.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Sunday Mass is offered at three times, and the 10 am Mass is at the Holy Spirit worship site, so check the schedule for the right church before you go. The online registration asks for household details and whether each person is baptized, confirmed or has received Holy Communion, with yes, no or unsure as answers.
first_visit_tips: Call the rectory at 215-468-4777 if you are not sure which church to attend on Sunday.
The parish office is open Monday to Thursday from 9 am to 2 pm and Friday from 9 am to 12 pm.
Holy day Masses are announced ahead of time, so check before a holy day.

records.notes: The parish's Mass page gives no holy day times, so the tier 1 archdiocese holy day times (8:30 am, 12:05 pm, 7 pm) are replaced by 'holy days announced'. The faith formation page returned 404, so PREP details come from the home and About pages only, and the program's schedule and age range are not recorded. The About page says the Holy Spirit and St. Richard parishes merged in 2014. The Holy Spirit worship site has no address on the site, so it is not added as a location.

records.name: St. Rita of Cascia Shrine
records.summary: A Catholic shrine at Broad and Ellsworth Streets with weekday, Saturday and Sunday Masses, a healing Mass once a month from September to May, and a Wednesday novena. Visitors can see the upper and lower shrines during posted hours.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, the monthly healing Mass, or the Wednesday novena to St. Rita, or visit the shrine during its posted hours. You can also ask about volunteering. Confession is offered on weekdays.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm, Sunday Mass at 10 am, and weekday Masses at 8 am and noon. Healing Mass at noon on the third Sunday of each month from September to May. Confession on weekdays at 10:45 am and 4 pm. Wednesday novena to St. Rita.

access.notes: An elevator serves both the upper and lower shrines. It is in the glassed-in lobby at the end of the breezeway, to the left of the Broad Street entrance. Nearest SEPTA: the Broad Street Line to the Ellsworth/Federal stop, and the shrine is on the west side.

first_step.how: Come to a listed Mass or to the Wednesday novena, or stop by during visiting hours. Call 215-546-8333 to ask about volunteering, since the shrine asks volunteers to use its form.
first_step.basis: Mass, the novena and the shrine are open to visitors and pilgrims, and the site invites people to volunteer through a form. The site describes no newcomer program or orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: The upper and lower shrines are open to visitors during posted hours, and the site lists no admission fee. The monthly healing Mass, held at noon on the third Sunday from September to May, includes an anointing with holy oil, the novena prayers and a veneration of the relic of St. Rita. The site says anyone seeking healing is welcome, and the shrine office keeps weekday and Saturday hours.
first_visit_tips: Park in the C.A.T.C.H. lot on 15th Street for weekend Mass, or use the two-hour street parking on Broad Street.
Do not park in turn lanes or on striped pavement, because you may be ticketed or towed.
Use the elevator in the glassed-in lobby, to the left of the Broad Street entrance, to reach both shrines.
Visiting hours are Monday to Friday 7:45 am to 5 pm, Saturday 7:45 am to 6 pm, and Sunday 9 am to 2 pm (the upper shrine closes at 11:15 am on Sunday).

records.notes: The shrine's Mass schedule and prayer pages returned 404, so the weekday and Saturday Mass times, confession times and Wednesday novena are carried over from the tier 1 archdiocese listing and were not re-read on the shrine site. The shrine site's phone is 215-546-8333, which replaces the tier 1 number 215-334-0159; the tier 1 number may belong to another office. The home page lists an October 18, 2026 healing Mass and a November 15, 2026 healing Mass, which is the basis for last_sign_of_life. Gift shop and shrine office hours are on the visit page and are not recorded here. The site has no newcomer program.

records.name: St. Thomas Aquinas Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 17th and Morris Streets in South Philadelphia with Masses in Vietnamese, English, Indonesian and Spanish. It describes itself as a multicultural, multilingual parish.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in the language you prefer, or pray in the Adoration Room. The Wednesday novena to Our Lady of Perpetual Help is at 7 pm in the chapel.

schedule.text: Saturday Masses at 4 pm (English) and 6 pm (Spanish). Sunday Masses at 8 am (Vietnamese), 10 am (English), noon (Indonesian) and 5 pm (Spanish). Daily Mass at 8:30 am (English) in the Aquinas Center, and at 8:30 am in the church on holy days. Confession before Mass, and Saturday 3:30 to 4 pm. Wednesday novena at 7 pm. The Adoration Room is open weekdays 9 am to 3:30 pm and on weekends 9 am to noon (archdiocese listing, not on the parish site).

first_step.how: Come to any Mass in the language you want, or call the parish at 215-334-2312 to ask about joining the parish or receiving the sacraments.
first_step.basis: The parish says it serves immigrants and people of many languages, and it invites people who want to join the parish or receive sacraments to call. The site has no newcomer welcome or orientation, so the rating is 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and it is held in four languages, so you can attend in English, Vietnamese, Indonesian or Spanish. The English Mass on Sunday is at 10 am and the daily English Mass is at 8:30 am. The Adoration Room is a quiet prayer space; the archdiocese listing gives its hours, but the parish site does not.
first_visit_tips: Choose the Mass by language: Vietnamese at 8 am, English at 10 am, Indonesian at noon, and Spanish at 5 pm on Sunday.
Confession is available before Mass or by appointment, so call the office if you want a set time.
The site does not list parking, transit or wheelchair access, so call 215-334-2312 before you come if you need those details.

records.notes: The parish site gives Mass times that differ from tier 1: a 4 pm English vigil, a 6 pm Spanish vigil, a 5 pm Spanish Mass on Sunday, an 8 am Vietnamese Mass (tier 1 left the am or pm unclear), and a daily 8:30 am English Mass in the Aquinas Center (address not on the site). These replace the tier 1 weekday times. The site lists no Adoration Room hours, novena details or Saturday confession time; those are carried over from the archdiocese listing and were not re-read. The site's contact, about and ministries pages returned 404 at guessed addresses, so the newcomer path rests on the home page.

notes: Batch of 7 parishes; all 7 published. Several guessed subpages returned 404 (St. Paul's and St. Thomas Aquinas had the most); 404s are not counted as blocked. The St. Peter the Apostle site returned HTTP 500 throughout, so its record uses the March 22, 2026 bulletin hosted on spaphilly.org (read as PDF) and the archdiocese listing from tier 1. The single WebSearch was used on St. Peter's. The search result also contained an unrelated formatting reminder that I did not act on. Mistake: I made one out-of-scope call to a Claude Docs read tool with a placeholder URL; it was refused and changed nothing. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used; 38 WebFetch calls used (cap 60; no group exceeded 6). Tier 1 facts that I could not re-read on the group's own site (archdiocese-sourced times and prices) are kept and labeled in each record's notes.
